text:
GMP carried out their blitz on crime across Salford on Thursday(Image: GMP)

Clouds of sawdust rose up over the streets of Salford as police sawed down the door of an alleged drug dealer in a block of flats near the River Irwell.

Passersby craned their necks and captured the scene on their phones as the tactical officers broke down the door with a battering ram and ran inside. All they're met with, however, is an extensive assortment of pet birds.

The suspect narrowly misses out on being part of the string of arrests made yesterday (June 11) in the district as part of Operation AVRO, a blitz on crime that Greater Manchester Police carries out every month in a different district.

Elsewhere in the region, GMP found 31 tasers, a firearm, a cannabis farm, stolen jewellery, a zombie knife, a dangerous dog, and a 'large amount of Class A & B' drugs. Almost £40k in cash was also found, including £35k located at one address.

Police found a cannabis farm in Salford during Operation AVRO(Image: GMP)

Police started the day at 6am, making arrests as Salford was slowly waking up. In total, 43 people were arrested and ten out of 14 warrants were positively executed.

Speaking to the Manchester Evening News, DCI Martyn Johnson said: "We're really showing the full breadth of policing, both proactively and with community engagement as well. The majority of what you see, particularly in terms of warrants, it's about us reacting to what the community is telling us is a problem in their area.

"If they tell us it's a problem or we find out it's a problem, we back it up with intelligence and then we'll take action against it, and that's what we've done this morning. It's a great thing, we listen to communities, we work with communities and we get good outcomes because of it.

"We want as many members of the public to come and see us as possible. When I talk to them and tell them about what we're doing, that's how you build up confidence with people and it's how you build up community relations.

"From that, the confidence comes that people will talk to us and if they've got a problem in their area, we'll take action like we have done with the warrants."

Operation AVRO in Salford(Image: GMP)

He added that as part of the operation's efforts, GMP hosted community events, such as the tri-service water safety event held at Salford Quays, community events at the Elsmere Centre in Walkden, and a retail crime initiative in Eccles town centre.

GMP also performed a traffic operation throughout the day, despite extremely persistent rain showers, which resulted in three vehicles being seized.

Almost 30 traffic offence reports were handed out for a mixture of reasons, including people not wearing seatbelts, driving without insurance, driving whilst using a mobile phone and having illegally tinted windows.

Moving forward, GMP says it wants to build on the community side of the operation, using different tactics to engage with people.

DCI Johnson added: "We'll build on the community engagement side, we'll use different tactics to engage people, different themes of policing as well. We've done retail crime today, but next time we might choose something different.

"Cyber crime's always big for us and we'll look at how we can engage with businesses instead. In terms of the warrants, if we get the intelligence, we'll do as many as we possibly can in a day. That's our commitment to the public, we will execute as many warrants as we can and get big results by doing it."
